news.headline: Rivalry among TMC factions in focus as parties gear up for Bengal civic polls
news.story_lead: Rivalry among TMC factions in focus as parties gear up for Bengal civic polls West Bengal civic polls are set to see a contest involving rival Trinamool Congress factions, the BJP and Congress as parties prepare for elections in Kolkata and Howrah. Rivalry between the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC), the Democratic Trinamool Congress (DTC) and the faction of Trinamool MPs who have joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) intensified on Friday as parties in West Bengal geared up for the municipal elections scheduled for Kolkata and Howrah in November. The parties said poll notifications were likely to be issued within a few days, leaving little time for candidate selection and campaigning.
news.full_article_text: Rivalry among TMC factions in focus as parties gear up for Bengal civic polls West Bengal civic polls are set to see a contest involving rival Trinamool Congress factions, the BJP and Congress as parties prepare for elections in Kolkata and Howrah. Rivalry between the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC), the Democratic Trinamool Congress (DTC) and the faction of Trinamool MPs who have joined the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) intensified on Friday as parties in West Bengal geared up for the municipal elections scheduled for Kolkata and Howrah in November. The parties said poll notifications were likely to be issued within a few days, leaving little time for candidate selection and campaigning. “Local leaders loyal to Mamata Banerjee will receive priority during candidate selection. There may be some talks on seat adjustment with the Congress if the situation demands but it is too early to speak on that,” a leader from the Mamata camp said, requesting anonymity after a meeting at the former chief minister’s residence in Kalighat. “Although Congress state committees select municipal poll nominees, issues such as alliances are decided by our central leaders. No such talks have taken place so far,” Pradesh Congress general secretary Asutosh Chatterjee said. Kunal Ghosh, a Kolkata MLA from the Mamata faction, targeted the NCPI, a self-declared ally of the Bharatiya Janata Party-led National Democratic Alliance government. Ghosh posted a photo of wall graffiti in which the face of Kolkata North Lok Sabha member Sudip Bandopadhyay — the leader of the Trinamool MPs who joined the NCPI — was covered with black paint. In the graffiti found in a neighbourhood in Shyambazar, Bandopadhyay was flanked by Union home minister Amit Shah and state BJP president Samik Bhattacharya. The graffiti featuring the two BJP leaders was untouched. “I don’t know who disfigured the graffiti but whoever did should not spare the other traitors in our party,” Ghosh said. The DTC, led by Ritabrata Banerjee, announced that it would not form an alliance with the NCPI. “We are the real Trinamool. We will contest on our own,” DTC president Arup Roy said after a party meeting. On October 20, the 20 former Trinamool MPs in the NCPI sought more time from Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to respond to petitions filed by the MAITC seeking their disqualification from the Lower House. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which controls 209 of Bengal’s 294 Assembly seats, held its first preparatory meeting in the presence of central leaders in Kolkata on Friday. “Our candidates will be selected based on their proven performance. People from other parties will not be entertained,” said Union minister of state Sukanta Majumdar, who is heading the BJP’s election committee for the Kolkata polls. The NCPI had earlier expressed eagerness to contest the civic body polls as a BJP ally, but Majumdar said his party would contest all the seats. On Friday, Majumdar also ruled out fielding Trinamool councillors who won the last election if they switched camps now. The civic bodies in both Kolkata and Howrah are being run by state-appointed administrators. The Trinamool councillors and the mayor resigned in Kolkata in May following the party’s defeat to the BJP in the Assembly polls. No election has been held in the Howrah Municipal Corporation since 2018 because of complications arising from delimitation rules. “The BJP will not have allies. Our candidates will contest all seats,” Ritesh Tiwari, co-convenor of the BJP’s four-member poll committee for Kolkata, told HT. In August this year, the West Bengal Legislative Assembly passed two bills to increase the number of civic wards from 144 to 209 in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) area and from 50 to 68 under the Howrah Municipal Corporation’s (HMC) jurisdiction. Presenting the bills in the Assembly, state urban development and municipal affairs minister Agnimitra Paul said delimitation would create smaller wards with lower populations, making the delivery of civic services to citizens faster and easier. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Tanmay Chatterjee Tanmay Chatterjee has spent more than three decades covering regional and national politics, internal security, intelligence, defence and corruption. news.headline: Tragic Collision on Jaipur-Ajmer Highway Claims 3 Lives, Injures 7 Maharashtra Pilgrims
news.story_lead: Three pilgrims from Maharashtra were killed on the spot and seven others sustained injuries when their bus collided with a trailer on the Jaipur-Ajmer National Highway in Rajasthan's Jaipur district. The bus was carrying 28 devotees who were traveling toward Chittorgarh after visiting the Khatushyamji shrine.
news.full_article_text:
In a tragic road accident in the early hours of Saturday around 1:50 AM, three pilgrims lost their lives and seven others were injured on the Jaipur-Ajmer National Highway near the Bagru area in Jaipur district. A private bus carrying 28 pilgrims from Nashik, Maharashtra, collided with a trailer while descending the Bagru culvert. Local police reported that the trailer was on fire at the time of the collision.

The group of devotees was traveling from the Khatushyamji temple to the Sanwariya Seth (Sanwalia Seth) temple located in Chittorgarh. Due to the impact, passengers seated in the front section of the bus suffered serious injuries. Local residents along with police personnel conducted rescue operations to extract those trapped in the wreckage. The deceased were identified as Mahendra (38), Sandeep (45), and Deepak (47).

All seven injured individuals were rushed to the trauma facility at Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Hospital in Jaipur for medical treatment. According to medical authorities, two of the injured were admitted in critical condition, three were kept under close observation, and two were discharged after receiving first aid. Police under Bagru Station House Officer Chandrabhan have launched an investigation into the precise cause of the accident.

In a separate incident on the preceding Friday around 6:00 AM, four friends from Agra, Uttar Pradesh, were killed and two others injured when their car plunged into a ditch following a tyre burst on National Highway 148 (Dausa-Manoharpur) in the Raisar area of Jaipur district. The victims were also returning from the Khatushyamji shrine.

Three pilgrims—Mahendra (38), Sandeep (45), and Deepak (47)—died on the spot.
Seven injured passengers were transported to the trauma center at SMS Hospital in Jaipur.
The pilgrims were traveling to the Sanwariya Seth temple in Chittorgarh after visiting Khatushyamji.
Bagru police reported that the trailer involved in the collision was on fire at the time of the crash.
In another crash on Friday on NH-148, four Agra residents died after a tyre burst sent their car into a ditch near Raisar.

Fatalities and Injuries: 3 deceased (Mahendra, Sandeep, Deepak) and 7 injured treated at SMS Hospital.

hindi_translation.headline: जयपुर-अजमेर हाईवे पर भीषण हादसा: महाराष्ट्र के 3 श्रद्धालुओं की मौत, 7 घायल
hindi_translation.story_lead: राजस्थान के जयपुर जिले में जयपुर-अजमेर राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग पर श्रद्धालुओं से भरी एक बस के ट्रॉले से टकरा जाने से महाराष्ट्र के तीन श्रद्धालुओं की मौके पर ही मौत हो गई और सात अन्य घायल हो गए। बस में 28 श्रद्धालु सवार थे जो खाटूश्यामजी के दर्शन के बाद चित्तौड़गढ़ जा रहे थे।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
शनिवार तड़के करीब 1:50 बजे जयपुर जिले के बगरू क्षेत्र में जयपुर-अजमेर राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग पर एक दर्दनाक सड़क हादसा हुआ, जिसमें तीन श्रद्धालुओं की मौत हो गई और सात अन्य घायल हो गए। महाराष्ट्र के नासिक से 28 श्रद्धालुओं को ले जा रही एक निजी बस बगरू पुलिया से उतरते समय एक ट्रॉले से टकरा गई। पुलिस के अनुसार, टक्कर के समय ट्रॉले में आग लगी हुई थी।

श्रद्धालुओं का दल खाटूश्यामजी मंदिर के दर्शन के बाद चित्तौड़गढ़ स्थित सांवलिया सेठ मंदिर जा रहा था। टक्कर इतनी तेज थी कि बस के अगले हिस्से में बैठे यात्रियों को गंभीर चोटें आईं। स्थानीय निवासियों और पुलिसकर्मियों ने बचाव अभियान चलाकर मलबे में फंसे लोगों को बाहर निकाला। मृतकों की पहचान महेंद्र (38), संदीप (45) और दीपक (47) के रूप में हुई है।

सभी सात घायलों को इलाज के लिए जयपुर के सवाई मानसिंह (एसएमएस) अस्पताल के ट्रॉमा सेंटर में भर्ती कराया गया। चिकित्सा अधिकारियों के अनुसार, दो घायलों की हालत नाजुक होने के कारण उन्हें भर्ती किया गया, तीन को निगरानी वार्ड में रखा गया और दो को प्राथमिक उपचार के बाद छुट्टी दे दी गई। बगरू थानाधिकारी चंद्रभान के नेतृत्व में पुलिस ने हादसे के कारणों की जांच शुरू कर दी है।

एक अन्य घटना में, शुक्रवार सुबह करीब 6:00 बजे जयपुर जिले के रायसर क्षेत्र में राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग 148 (दौसा-मनोहरपुर) पर टायर फटने के बाद कार खाई में गिरने से उत्तर प्रदेश के आगरा के चार दोस्तों की मौत हो गई और दो अन्य घायल हो गए। ये सभी भी खाटूश्यामजी के दर्शन कर लौट रहे थे।
bullet_points: नासिक से 28 श्रद्धालुओं को ले जा रही एक बस बगरू पुलिया पर जयपुर-अजमेर हाईवे पर एक ट्रॉले से टकरा गई।
हादसे में तीन श्रद्धालुओं—महेंद्र (38), संदीप (45) और दीपक (47) की मौके पर ही मौत हो गई।
सात घायल यात्रियों को जयपुर के एसएमएस अस्पताल के ट्रॉमा सेंटर में भर्ती कराया गया।
श्रद्धालु खाटूश्यामजी के दर्शन के बाद चित्तौड़गढ़ स्थित सांवलिया सेठ मंदिर जा रहे थे।
बगरू पुलिस ने बताया कि टक्कर के समय दुर्घटनाग्रस्त ट्रॉले में आग लगी हुई थी।
शुक्रवार को एनएच-148 पर रायसर के पास टायर फटने से हुई एक अन्य कार दुर्घटना में आगरा के चार लोगों की मौत हो गई।
key_facts: घटना स्थल: बगरू पुलिया, जयपुर-अजमेर राष्ट्रीय राजमार्ग, जयपुर जिला, राजस्थान।
यात्रियों का मार्ग: नासिक (महाराष्ट्र) के श्रद्धालु, खाटूश्यामजी से सांवलिया सेठ मंदिर (चित्तौड़गढ़) की यात्रा पर।

news.story_lead: Satellite-tagged Amur falcons complete round-trip migration across 23 countries, return to Manipur Satellite-tagged Amur falcons Apapang and Alang have returned to Manipur after covering nearly 20,000 km across 23 countries on their round-trip migration. news.full_article_text: Satellite-tagged Amur falcons complete round-trip migration across 23 countries, return to Manipur Satellite-tagged Amur falcons Apapang and Alang have returned to Manipur after covering nearly 20,000 km across 23 countries on their round-trip migration. After travelling across 23 countries and covering nearly 20,000 km, two satellite-tagged Amur falcons, Apapang and Alang, have returned to Manipur, completing a round-trip migration that included a six-day, non-stop flight of nearly 6,000 km between northeast India and Somalia in Africa, Union environment ministry officials said on Friday. The birds, which were tagged by Wildlife Institute of India scientists in November 2025, arrived from China on Thursday and are expected to spend the next two to three weeks at selected sites in the mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district before embarking on their next long-haul flight. Manipur, along with other parts of northeast India, serves as an important stopover for the migratory birds, which feed on termites to accumulate fat reserves for their next leg of the journey — a nearly 6,000-km flight to Somalia, including a 3,000-km crossing over the Arabian Sea. Apapang and Alang, along with a third falcon named Ahu, were fitted with satellite transmitters by scientists from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) at the Chiuluan roosting site in Tamenglong district in November 2025. While tracking signals from Apapang and Alang confirmed their return to Manipur, scientists lost contact with Ahu somewhere in Somalia earlier this year. “The two Amur falcons are expected to now make a two to three week stopover at select sites in the beautiful mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district in Manipur, where local people now eagerly wait for their return year after year and protect the falcons,” environment minister Bhupender Yadav said in a post on X on Friday. Yadav said the successful completion of the birds’ full round-trip journey marked an important milestone. “The two Amur falcons are expected to now make a two to three week stopover at select sites in the beautiful mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district in Manipur, where local people now eagerly wait for their return year after year and protect the falcons,” said Yadav on X. Amur falcons typically spend their winter in southern Africa, reaching there between November and December and staying until March or April before returning to their breeding grounds in northern China and Siberia by April and May. They are primarily insectivores, feeding on termites, ants, locusts and beetles, but can also consume mice, smaller birds and lizards. Officials at the Union environment ministry said the Amur falcon tracking project began in 2013, initially in Nagaland, as a conservation effort to address the issue of hunting at stopover sites in northeast India. Ramesh Pandey, additional director general of forests at the environment ministry, said that, with the active participation of local people, the project provides unique insights into the species, particularly their non-stop, long-distance flights of nearly 6,000 km in six days from northeast India to Somalia. “With the falcons returning back a year later and few making round-trip journeys multiple times to the stopover sites in Nagaland, this created the desired awareness among local people and a sense of ownership began. This also resulted in hunters turning protectors, leading to complete protection of this migratory falcon,” he said. Pandey said that, to continue the conservation efforts, another phase of satellite tagging was carried out in 2016 across stopover sites in Nagaland. The success of the initiative spread to neighbouring Manipur and Assam, where Amur falcons began to receive protection at the stopover sites as well. Amur falcons have been tagged in 2019, 2024 and 2025, with the latest tagging taking place in November 2025, when three such falcons were tagged in Manipur. “The successful tracking of Amur falcons has provided much needed information on where and how long they stop over in northeast India, and also as to how super-abundant termite prey availability in and around the stopover sites has shaped their migration strategies,” Pandey said. He added that in southern Africa, in the southern hemisphere, the Amurs spend nearly three months during the southern summer in Botswana, Zimbabwe and South Africa. Similarly, their breeding sites in northeastern China and the Russian Far East are also well mapped, he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. His reports in 2019 on toxic leachate from Delhi's landfills led to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) taking suo motu cognisance and ultimately asking the state government to start bio-mining to flatten and remove all three landfills in the capital. He also closely tracks the implementation of government policies on climate, renewable energy and environmental protection. After travelling across 23 countries and covering nearly 20,000 km, two satellite-tagged Amur falcons, Apapang and Alang, have returned to Manipur, completing a round-trip migration that included a six-day, non-stop flight of nearly 6,000 km between northeast India and Somalia in Africa, Union environment ministry officials said on Friday.

The birds, which were tagged by Wildlife Institute of India scientists in November 2025, arrived from China on Thursday and are expected to spend the next two to three weeks at selected sites in the mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district before embarking on their next long-haul flight.

Manipur, along with other parts of northeast India, serves as an important stopover for the migratory birds, which feed on termites to accumulate fat reserves for their next leg of the journey — a nearly 6,000-km flight to Somalia, including a 3,000-km crossing over the Arabian Sea.

Apapang and Alang, along with a third falcon named Ahu, were fitted with satellite transmitters by scientists from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) at the Chiuluan roosting site in Tamenglong district in November 2025. While tracking signals from Apapang and Alang confirmed their return to Manipur, scientists lost contact with Ahu somewhere in Somalia earlier this year.

“The two Amur falcons are expected to now make a two to three week stopover at select sites in the beautiful mountainous tracts of Tamenglong district in Manipur, where local people now eagerly wait for their return year after year and protect the falcons,” environment minister Bhupender Yadav said in a post on X on Friday.
Yadav said the successful completion of the birds’ full round-trip journey marked an important milestone.

Amur falcons typically spend their winter in southern Africa, reaching there between November and December and staying until March or April before returning to their breeding grounds in northern China and Siberia by April and May. They are primarily insectivores, feeding on termites, ants, locusts and beetles, but can also consume mice, smaller birds and lizards. Officials at the Union environment ministry said the Amur falcon tracking project began in 2013, initially in Nagaland, as a conservation effort to address the issue of hunting at stopover sites in northeast India. Ramesh Pandey, additional director general of forests at the environment ministry, said that, with the active participation of local people, the project provides unique insights into the species, particularly their non-stop, long-distance flights of nearly 6,000 km in six days from northeast India to Somalia. “With the falcons returning back a year later and few making round-trip journeys multiple times to the stopover sites in Nagaland, this created the desired awareness among local people and a sense of ownership began. This also resulted in hunters turning protectors, leading to complete protection of this migratory falcon,” he said. Pandey said that, to continue the conservation efforts, another phase of satellite tagging was carried out in 2016 across stopover sites in Nagaland. The success of the initiative spread to neighbouring Manipur and Assam, where Amur falcons began to receive protection at the stopover sites as well. Amur falcons have been tagged in 2019, 2024 and 2025, with the latest tagging taking place in November 2025, when three such falcons were tagged in Manipur. “The successful tracking of Amur falcons has provided much needed information on where and how long they stop over in northeast India, and also as to how super-abundant termite prey availability in and around the stopover sites has shaped their migration strategies,” Pandey said.
